statement: An injective fibration or trivial fibration has every component a fibration or trivial fibration, respectively.
repair: Apply the preceding corollary to each object inclusion e->I.

statement: The converse componentwise condition for injective fibrations need not hold.
repair: False converse is exhibited by the walking-arrow Set example and by the explicit matching-map criterion.

statement: An injectively fibrant diagram has fibrant values.
repair: Apply the componentwise fibration assertion to X->*.

statement: Restriction preserves homotopy cocartesian squares and suspension exact sequences.
repair: With the established uniform model structures, restriction is homotopical and left Quillen; in the associated derivator it is exact in the independent diagram variable.

statement: Restriction also preserves homotopy cartesian squares and cosuspension exact sequences.
repair: True for the associated model derivator because restriction between shifted derivators preserves homotopy Kan extensions.

statement: The ordinary functor u_* preserves arbitrary homotopy cartesian squares merely because it preserves F and TF.
gap_or_error: An ordinary right Quillen functor is homotopical on fibrant objects, not on arbitrary inputs. The author retracts the unqualified inference on pp.49–50.
repair: Apply the assertion to its right derived functor, or first make the necessary fibrant replacements. The two-vertex contractible-groupoid cospan gives an explicit failure of strict-limit homotopy invariance.

statement: A right homotopy Kan extension generally does not preserve homotopy cocartesian squares.
repair: For a discrete two-object shape, the derived product takes the homotopy coproduct of (S^1,*) and (*,S^1) to the torus, whereas the coproduct of their products is S^1 wedge S^1; fundamental groups differ.
notes: This supplies the requested example with finite poset indexing categories.

statement: The ordinary u_! should preserve arbitrary homotopy cocartesian squares.
gap_or_error: The source immediately questions this assertion and distinguishes ordinary from derived functors.
repair: The two-interval span and its collapse to two points are objectwise weakly equivalent but have strict pushouts S^1 and *. The left derived u_! has the expected preservation property.

statement: Ordinary u_! and u_* need not preserve the objectwise weak equivalences and must be distinguished from adjoints on the localized categories.
repair: Both failures are worked out explicitly in the commentary.

statement: Do the preceding assumptions ensure the existence of homotopy adjoints u_!^W and u_*^W, even for finite posets?
repair: Under the uniform closed exact structures, right adjoints are derived by Ken Brown; under combinatorial structures both exist for all small u. The broader earlier recognition problem is separate.
references: Hovey1999, Definition 1.3.6 and Lemma 1.3.10; Barwick2007, Proposition 1.22
notes: Open records the author’s unresolved question at this point, not current open status in the combinatorial case.

statement: If X is injectively fibrant and alpha:s->t is monic in I, then X(alpha):X(t)->X(s) belongs to F.
repair: The comma components for the functor [1]->I are singletons or single arrows because alpha is monic; restriction preserves fibrancy and the walking-arrow criterion applies. Full argument supplied.

statement: A presheaf X=(X1->X0) on [1] is injectively fibrant if and only if X0,X1 are fibrant and X1->X0 belongs to F.
repair: The matching-map criterion proves it; X1 fibrant is redundant once X0 fibrant and X1->X0 a fibration are known.
notes: Source footnote refers ahead to p.63, outside this attachment.

statement: For a sieve j:I-prime->I and injectively fibrant X, the map lim_I X -> lim_I-prime j^*X belongs to F, whenever these limits exist.
repair: For a: A->B in TC, the relative constant diagram const A amalgam_(j_!const A) j_!const B -> const B is objectwise a or identity; lifting against X proves the assertion. Full proof in commentary.

statement: A relative category is quillenizable when it admits an exact weak Quillen structure.

statement: Quillenizability so defined is self-dual.
repair: Opposition exchanges C with F and TC with TF; exact factorization reverses correspondingly.

statement: W is quillenizable on a full domain Diag of small categories when every (M(I),W(I)) is quillenizable.
Diag is intended to contain finite posets and to be closed under finite limits and finite coproducts, possibly finite colimits.

statement: The accessible situation of sections 3–4 provides quillenizability on all small categories.

statement: Localizing the category of cochain complexes in an abelian category A at quasi-isomorphisms gives D(A).

statement: The bounded-below, bounded-above, and bounded subcategories have the induced quasi-isomorphisms and their corresponding derived localizations.

statement: Ch^{>=0} consists of complexes vanishing in negative degrees, and Ch^{<=0} of complexes vanishing in positive degrees.

repair: Use the editors’ explicit correction i<0 and i>0; preserve both readings in the source.

statement: If A has enough projectives, (Ch^-(A),quasi-isomorphisms) is quillenizable.
repair: Dual bounded-above projective construction.

statement: The unbounded derived category can be defined without assuming enough injective or projective objects.
repair: Verdier localization provides the construction at the relevant universe level; this is not itself a theorem of existence of resolutions or derived adjoints.

statement: What quillenization or derived-functor theory is available for unbounded complexes in a general abelian category?
repair: Modules, sheaves, and Grothendieck abelian categories have unbounded resolutions; a claim for every abelian category needs additional hypotheses and size control.
references: Spaltenstein1988, Theorems C and D; StacksKInjectives, tag 079P; CisinskiDeglise2009, Theorem 1.2

statement: Ch(A) is small if and only if A is small.
repair: Complexes are countable sequences of objects and arrows from a set; conversely A embeds as degree-zero complexes. Interpret small up to the same chosen universe.

statement: If A is accessible and has filtered colimits, Ch(A) has the corresponding accessibility and filtered-colimit properties.
repair: Filtered colimits are calculated degreewise; the category of complexes is an accessible category of diagrams with equations.
notes: The unqualified etc. cannot include the variable-bound categories below.

statement: The same filtered-colimit closure holds for Ch^+(A), Ch^-(A), and Ch^b(A).

statement: A Grothendieck abelian category has enough injectives.
repair: A standard existence theorem; the stronger K-injective theorem also supplies injective resolutions.

statement: For the Grothendieck abelian situation, Ch^+(A) is quillenizable on all small indexing categories.

statement: For Grothendieck A, right derived Kan extension sends D^+(A(I-prime)) to D^+(A(I)) and is right adjoint to restriction.

statement: Does the right derived Kan extension exist on the whole unbounded derived category?

statement: A left homotopy Kan extension need not preserve D^+ without a homological-dimension restriction.

statement: For Grothendieck A, a left derived Kan extension is expected on D^-(A(I-prime)) with values in D^-(A(I)).

notes: Enough projectives in A is not required merely to use a projective model structure on the diagram category of complexes.

statement: Does left derived Kan extension exist on all of D(A(I-prime)) without finite cohomological dimension?

statement: Any relative category gives a prederivator I -> M(I)[W(I)^{-1}], when the indicated localizations and universe conventions are available.

statement: HO_{M,W}(I), HO_W(I), and D_{M,W}(I) denote the same localized diagram category.

statement: Restriction functors are exact for these fibre/cofibre structures.

statement: Which derivator axioms follow from quillenizability alone?

General closed model categories with the required small limits and colimits yield derivators; closure and completeness conventions must be checked before applying that modern theorem.

statement: For a finite family of shapes, HO_W(coproduct I_alpha) is equivalent to the product of HO_W(I_alpha), without quillenizability.
repair: Relative categories split as a finite product; coordinate arrows commute and finite zigzags can be padded to show localization commutes with that finite product. Full argument supplied.

statement: If W is strongly saturated and the diagram category has the stated representation property from quillenization, evaluations jointly detect isomorphisms in HO_W(I).
repair: Represent a localized arrow by an actual map up to arrow-category isomorphism; invertibility at all evaluations puts every component in W, hence the natural transformation in W(I).

statement: Every arrow of HO_W(I) is isomorphic, as an arrow, to the localization of a genuine morphism of M(I).

statement: The chosen fundamental localizer is proposed to satisfy all seven good axioms referenced in Chapter XII.

statement: Uniform left quillenization will yield right homotopy direct images for suitable u.

statement: u_* carries fibrant diagrams to fibrant diagrams.

If every comma category I-prime/s is admissible, u is admissible, provided these shapes and restrictions are in the stipulated domain.
repair: When the requisite fibre coproducts exist, the slice projection has left Kan extension by coproducts of values, so restriction preserves fibrancy; then apply slice admissibility pointwise. statement: When I is a poset, each projection I-prime/s -> I-prime identifies its domain with a sieve.

statement: When I is a poset, admissibility of u also implies admissibility of the slice shapes.

statement: Every finite poset is admissible for the given uniform left quillenization.

repair: Opposition exchanges upper and lower sets, hence opens and closed sets in the two Alexandrov conventions.

statement: The preceding preservation results for restrictions, right Kan extensions and fibrant arrows remain valid under uniform left quillenisability without separately assuming exactness on the left.
repair: The relevant lifting adjunction arguments are given in commentary; fibrant restriction along local isomorphisms requires the applicable left-Kan/coproduct hypotheses.
notes: Source invokes Proposition1p45 and corollaries through Proposition3p50.

statement: Uniform left structures are intended to yield right homotopy images, and uniform right structures to yield left homotopy images.
repair: Restriction is left Quillen in the first orientation and right Quillen in the second.
notes: Names refer to the objectwise lifting class, not the variance of the derived image.

statement: For u:I′→I, assume all limits of the comma shapes I′/s exist in M, so that ordinary u_*:M(I′)→M(I) exists.
repair: The finite case follows from finite limits in M0.
notes: Source’s varinjlim finies is a retained slip for varprojlim finies.

statement: Under uniform left quillenisability, u_* preserves fibrant objects.
repair: Since u* preserves TC, u_* preserves F by adjunction and preserves terminal objects.
notes: The earlier proposition is invoked; proof supplied in commentary.

statement: A functor u is left admissible when u_* preserves W between fibrant I′-diagrams. A shape Z is admissible when Z→e is.
repair: The Brown argument makes this automatic under the stated closed exact hypotheses whenever u_* exists.
notes: Terminology retained for reading the source.

statement: If every comma category I′/s is admissible and restriction to it preserves fibrant objects, then u is admissible.
repair: Compute each component of u_*f by its comma-category limit.
notes: The theorem states this tersely; preservation of fibrant restriction is the preceding local-isomorphism input.

statement: For a poset I the preceding slice criterion has a converse.
gap_or_error: No separate converse proof is given in this passage.
repair: Under the actual uniform closed exact hypotheses all the existing slice right images are admissible by Brown, so the asserted converse holds.
notes: Do not claim openness alone supplies a proof without its ambient hypotheses.

statement: Every finite poset is left admissible.
repair: The source gives an induction through a two-open cover and the pullback shape; Brown supplies a shorter general proof.
notes: The finite construction remains informative and valid.

statement: A poset I is admissible if the Alexandrov space I^op is noetherian and sober.
gap_or_error: The statement is true, but the suggested possibility of infinite examples is misleading: noetherian sober Alexandrov posets are finite.
repair: Complete proof of finiteness supplied in commentary; the source’s noetherian induction itself is valid.
notes: Do not flag the admissibility theorem as false; flag only its asserted enlargement of scope.

statement: Noetherianity of I^op means ACC on upper subsets of I, equivalently DCC on lower subsets; sobriety means every nonempty directed lower subset of I has a greatest element.
repair: These are the source’s Alexandrov order conventions.
notes: The directed-set formulation includes nonemptiness.
